chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, Fadalah ibn Ayyub, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about wiping with stones, and he said: “Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali عليه السلام used to wipe with three stones.”

key_terms.التَّمَسُّحِ: wiping or cleansing in this context after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّل: Imam al-Husayn عليه السلام, whose practice is cited as evidence

ai.seo_question: How many stones were used for cleansing according to the practice of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a ruling related to ritual purity and cleansing after relieving oneself. It reports the practice of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali عليه السلام, indicating the use of three stones for cleaning, which serves as evidence in jurisprudential discussions on istibra' and purification.
